role_in_parent: This is the new core structural input: it replaces the prior cyclotomic-positivity bottleneck by a weighted complete-intersection realization theorem.
statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

domain_restrictions: A,B,d are integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
Empty product convention: if d=0 then ∏_{i=1}^0 (...) = 1 so Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1
Assumption: the rational expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) is actually a polynomial, i.e., Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q] (not just a rational function)
Graded ring S is Q[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=B+i for i=1..d
If d=0, interpret S as Q (no variables, hence no f_i witnesses needed)
Each f_i is homogeneous in S with weighted degree deg(f_i)=A+i
Regularity condition: in the successive quotient S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}), the class of f_i is not a zero-divisor (equivalently: (f_1,...,f_d) is a homogeneous regular sequence in S)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Let A,B,d ∈ Z with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q_{A,B,d}(q)=∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) with Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1. If Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q], then in the weighted graded polynomial ring S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] (or S=Q if d=0) with deg(x_i)=B+i, there exist homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d ∈ S such that deg(f_i)=A+i for each i=1..d and for each i the class of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor (so f_1,...,f_d form a homogeneous regular sequence). Consequently, the graded data of S modulo this regular sequence yields the given expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) (as stated in the equivalence).
quantifier_order: For all integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) := ∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) belongs to Q[q] (q formal indeterminate)
There exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that for each i=1..d: deg(f_i)=A+i, and the image of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor

variables.name: A
variables.role: parameter controlling numerator degrees; constrained by A >= B >= 0

variables.name: B
variables.role: parameter controlling denominator degrees/variable weights; constrained by B <= A and B >= 0

variables.name: d
variables.role: length of the product/regular sequence; constrained by d >= 0

variables.name: Q_{A,B,d}(q)
variables.role: given expression prod_{i=1}^d (1-q^(A+i))/(1-q^(B+i)) assumed to lie in Q[q]
variables.type: rational function / formal expression in q

variables.domain: Q[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading (or Q if d=0)
variables.name: S
variables.role: ambient weighted polynomial ring where the f_i live

variables.name: f_i
variables.role: witnesses forming a homogeneous regular sequence; deg(f_i)=A+i

witness_dependencies: The witnesses f_1,...,f_d depend on the parameters (A,B,d) via the choice of the ambient weighted ring S and the required degrees deg(f_i)=A+i
The regularity (non-zero-divisor) condition is imposed sequentially on the images of f_i in the quotients by the previously chosen f_1,...,f_{i-1}
